Line: Ask me something easier, Little Ember.
[He hums a few notes of an old song, notices you listening, and stops.]
That's a big question for such a small ember. Ask me again another night.
[He tilts his head, smiling, and says nothing at all.]
I'll answer that when you answer one of mine.
Some sparks are better left where they fell. Leave this one.
Not that. Ask me something else.
[He starts to answer, then only shakes his head.]
[He pinches out a candle flame and watches the smoke rise.]
The Goddess teaches patience, child. So shall I.
[He studies you for a long moment, kind-eyed, and says nothing.]
Some questions are better laid before the Goddess than before a king.
Is that what you wish to ask me? Think again, child, and ask me better.
Let us leave that, child. The Goddess hears what we do not say.
[He smiles slowly, as if you had said something wise.]
[He folds his hands and waits, as though you had not finished speaking.]
Ha! You think I'd give that away for free? Bring me something better.
[She fiddles with the bells in her braid and pretends she didn't hear.]
Ask me after rehearsal. Or never. Never works too.
Darling, that's a question for someone who cares.
[She glances over her shoulder, then back at you, and smiles too brightly.]
Mm. Next question.
Did your feet ask that, or your mouth? Neither one is good enough yet.
Not your concern, dancer.
[He looks past you at the patrol and does not answer.]
I don't answer questions. I ask them.
Hm.
[He folds his arms and waits for you to say something sensible.]
Ask your troupe leader.
Mind your steps, dancer, not my business.
Forgive me, my lady, I couldn't say...
[He bows low and busies himself with the wine tray.]
[He glances toward the nobles and lets the sentence die before it starts.]
That's... perhaps not for a servant to answer, my lady.
More wine, my lady? Or coffee? I... must keep moving.
Please, my lady, the walls...
May she rise, child. The Goddess knows the answer, even when I do not.
[He touches the ash on his temples and murmurs a short prayer.]
Ask the flame, child. It listens better than an old priest.
Such questions are for the high priests, child. I only tend the flame.
[He smiles and blesses you with two fingers, as if that were an answer.]
Hm? Forgive me, child, my thoughts were... May she rise.
[He yawns.] Ask someone who's awake.
That one costs more than you've got, dancer.
Don't know. Don't care.
[He shrugs and stares at the wall.]
My shift's long enough without your questions.
[He rubs his thumb and fingers together and says nothing.]
Oh, sweetheart, you ask the funniest things!
[She smiles with her mouth only and turns away.]
[She laughs, light and empty, and fixes her bangles.]
Work it out yourself. The new girl is so clever, isn't she?
Mm, who knows? Certainly not me, sweetheart.
Why would I tell you? You'll have everything else soon enough.
